title: Parametrized mate core for internal adjunction evaluation
statement: The tensor-Hom transpose of the parametrized conjugate of the projection map is projection followed by tensor transpose and exceptional counit.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: evaluation and exceptional counit underlying the internal adjunction; see also prop-asd-internal-adjunction proof, displayed Hom bijections

proof.text: For arbitrary adjunctions a1 and a2 and a transformation alpha between their left adjoints, expand inverse Hom transposes as left-adjoint images followed by counits. Apply Mathlib conjugateEquiv_counit and naturality of alpha. This proves that the a2-transpose of h followed by the mate of alpha equals alpha followed by the a1-transpose of h.

Unfold only the finite-coefficient internal-adjunction isomorphism and its parametrized conjugate component. Its component is the mate of the given projection map for the composite of inverse-image, tensor-Hom, and exceptional adjunctions. Abstract the projection component and normalize its source and target functor types before applying the preceding identity; this avoids unfolding any derived-functor or compactification construction.

Expand the Hom equivalence of the composite adjunction using Adjunction.comp_homEquiv. Express the final exceptional transpose by Adjunction.homEquiv_counit, and reassociate. The result is projection followed by compact direct image of the inverse-image and tensor transposes, then the exceptional counit.

proof_origin.place: Displayed Hom-bijection calculation, formalized by conjugateEquiv_counit, naturality, and the composite adjunction Hom equivalence (B6).

split_report.summary: Expanded the canonical Hom-bijection construction and evaluated its action on an arbitrary map h. All ingredients are existing nodes; no new node, no changed statement, no Lean writing or compilation. Checked constant finite coefficients and unbounded ordinary etale typing, the proper/open projection normalization, and the direction of exceptional counit transposition.
